title: Book: The Essays of Warren Buffett — compiled by Lawrence Cunningham (1997)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: This book arranges Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters by topic. Recurring ideas: think of a share as part-ownership of a business and not a ticker; stay inside your 'circle of competence' and skip what you can't understand; insist on a margin of safety; buy good businesses at sensible prices and hold them for years; be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful; avoid leverage and fees; and be honest about mistakes. Buffett has also recommended low-cost index funds for people who do not want to research companies. Cautions: his results came from enormous capital, patience and skill, which are hard to copy, and examples are US-focused.
